sections.h2: Where is the Bucks County Recorder of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 55 East Court Street, 6th floor, in Doylestown, and the phone is 215-348-6209. It is open weekdays from 7:45 a.m. to 4:15 p.m., but every document to be recorded has to be submitted by 4 p.m. Papers that reach the counter after noon can slip to the following workday.

The Recorder keeps real estate records back to 1684, the era of the county's founding under William Penn. Besides deeds and mortgages, the office handles as many as 25 other kinds of documents, including subdivision plans, UCC filings, mausoleum and sewer permits, and notary commissions. Official records survive on microfiche, microfilm and PDF/A, and the office has stopped preparing bound books.

The county's assessment board works in step with the Recorder. Its deed registry staff check every document and attach tax parcel labels before recording, so a deed with a wrong parcel number or an old owner name can stall at that desk.

sections.h2: What will Bucks County charge to file a deed?
sections.html:
The county's schedule is built on one parcel, four names and four pages. Each page beyond four adds $4, each name beyond four adds $1, and each parcel beyond one adds $10. For the base amount on a deed or mortgage, use the recording fee calculator the county links, which was built by the state's recorders association. The Statement of Value form is not counted as a fee page.

Checks and money orders are made out to the Bucks County Recorder of Deeds. The calculators do not include certified copies, and staff verify final amounts when the document is recorded. Call 215-348-6209 to confirm a number before you send anything.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax do Bucks County sellers face?
sections.html:
The rate is 2%, split evenly between Harrisburg and the local taxing bodies, and the Recorder takes payment at the time of filing. The tax applies to the value of the interest conveyed, which is not always the sales price. Neither the state nor local governments say who pays, so most purchase agreements split it between buyer and seller. The new owner is on the hook if the amount paid turns out to be short.

Since January 2026 the office has refused personal checks for transfer tax. Accepted methods are cash in the office, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card. Title agents usually handle this at settlement, so confirm which method your closer will use.

  • Some transfers are exempt, such as conveyances between spouses, from parents to children, across three generations, and among siblings.
  • A one-time transfer between former spouses is allowed.
  • If an investigator finds a higher value, the state can bill extra tax and interest and mails the determination to you directly.
  • State revenue officials describe their share as 1% of the value, collected with any local tax by the county recorder.

sections.h2: When do you need a Statement of Value in Bucks County?
sections.html:
A Statement of Value, the state's REV-183 form, is needed whenever transfer tax is not paid or the true value is missing from the deed, as with a $1 consideration. It sets the value or gives the reason for an exemption. The county accepts only the June 2019 version of the form, and a paper copy must come in duplicate.

The form uses the Common Level Ratio Factor, which the county posts for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. State investigators later check whether the stated value or exemption holds up. If it does not, the state issues the determination and the extra tax and interest go to the state, with a receipt sent to the Recorder for recording.

For a deed recorded electronically, attachments such as a trust agreement, mortgage or assignment add a $1 per page copy fee. The office prints them for the Department of Revenue and then deletes them from the public record. Mailing those pages in on paper avoids the charge.

sections.h2: How can you submit a deed for recording in Bucks County?
sections.html:
You can e-record through Simplifile, CSC or ePN, bring the paper deed to the counter, or mail it. A mailed package needs the correct checks payable to the Recorder and a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself. Deeds, mortgages, general powers of attorney, satisfactions and copy requests should come straight to the Recorder's office.

The office stopped issuing book and page numbers on July 1, 2012, so every recorded document carries only an instrument number. Paper receipts ended in 2012 as well. Receipts now go by email, which requires the Submitter Information Form on file with the office.

  • Free services include the Fraud Alert System, which tells an owner if something is recorded against the property.
  • You can request a free email copy of your own deed.
  • Military discharge papers (DD-214) are recorded free.
  • In-office notary service is available.

sections.h2: What else should Bucks County sellers check before filing?
sections.html:
Bucks County is the northern edge of the Philadelphia area, covering 622 square miles between the Delaware River and Montgomery County, with Doylestown as its seat and Bensalem the largest township. Census Bureau estimates for 2020 to 2024 give $445,700 as the middle home value among owners, and 77.8% of households own. The county's 2020 population was 646,538.

On a house of that price, 2% transfer tax is a real line item, so settle early who bears it. Check that the municipality named on the deed matches the tax bill, since the local half of the tax depends on it. The assessment board says there is a gap between recording and updates on its public site, and it can be reached at 215-348-6219 for ownership questions.

Sellers who want a faster close can ask a cash buyer to handle the paperwork. Give the closing agent the parcel number, every owner name and the school district well before the settlement date.

faqs.q: What are the Bucks County Recorder of Deeds office hours?
faqs.a: Counter service runs weekdays, 7:45 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Documents to be recorded have to be submitted by 4 p.m. A package received after noon may wait for the following workday.

faqs.q: Can I pay Bucks County transfer tax with a personal check?
faqs.a: No. Since January 2026 the Recorder of Deeds does not take personal checks for realty transfer tax. Accepted methods are cash in the office, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card, and cards carry a 3.0% service fee.

faqs.q: What is the fee for each extra page on a Bucks County deed?
faqs.a: Each page after the fourth costs $4. Names after the fourth cost $1 each and parcels after the first cost $10 each. The REV-183 Statement of Value does not count as a fee page.

faqs.q: Does Bucks County require a Statement of Value?
faqs.a: Yes, when transfer tax is not paid or the deed does not show the true value, for example a $1 consideration. Use the June 2019 version of REV-183, in duplicate if submitted on paper. The state may later send a determination if the stated value looks low.

faqs.q: How far back do Bucks County deed records go?
faqs.a: The Recorder of Deeds holds records from 1684 to the present. They are kept on microfiche, microfilm and PDF/A, and the office does not prepare bound books anymore. Documents recorded since July 1, 2012 carry an instrument number only.
